title: Li Zicheng
capsule: Li Zicheng (李自成, 1606–1645) was a former postal station worker from Shaanxi who led the largest of the rebellions that brought down the Ming dynasty, proclaiming the short-lived Shun dynasty (大順) in Xi'an in January 1644 and capturing Beijing in April 1644 — at which point the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself, ending the Ming. Li's rule in Beijing lasted less than two months: the Ming general Wu Sangui allied with the Manchu Qing to defeat Li at the Battle of Shanhai Pass (27 May 1644), and Li was forced to abandon the capital within days. He was killed in June 1645 in Hubei under circumstances that remain debated — either by local militia or by his own hand — before he could consolidate any stable administration.
